orgDesign.domainName: Paramedical and Mental Health Practice Platform
orgDesign.companyProfile: Dutch healthcare software group modeled on Health Cloud Initiative (HCI, hci-software.com), formed by Vortex Capital Partners and founder Eric de Boer in a 2021 buyout of Incura and grown through more than 14 add-on acquisitions: CRS (GGZ EPD), FysioRoadmap, Winbase, Ensemble/Evry and Footfit/PodoFile (January 2023), NICE Software with paraNICE and NICE Connect (May 2023), Uw Zorg Online (June 2023), Quli (September 2023), Praktijkinfo (October 2023), Embloom (July 2024), SpotOnMedics (August 2024, from VvAA), plus Trompbx, LogicData/FysioLogic, Abakus and Edevop. The group supports more than 40,000 healthcare professionals every day and more than 4 million patients, describes itself since the SpotOnMedics acquisition as market leader in physiotherapy software ('1 in 4 paramedics'), reported EUR 20 million turnover in late 2023, is certified for NEN 7510 and ISO 27001, and employs about 250 people in the Netherlands and Switzerland; the organisation is modeled at 245 people. Marc Prette led the company as CEO from 2023; Robin Dunki Jacobs, who joined in 2024 as Business Unit Director responsible for integrating the labels, became CEO on 1 May 2025 with the mandate to integrate the acquired solutions into HCI One, expand digital patient access through a unified network, and invest in digital triage, AI and e-health. Revenue is recurring software subscriptions per practice or professional (custom-quoted on number of therapists, modules and integrations), billing services on declared turnover, e-health content licences and practice websites, on top of consumer-scale patient environments that are free for citizens and paid by care providers.
orgDesign.operatingModel: With about 245 people the group runs as four business units around its product families - Paramedical (HCI One, FysioRoadmap, SpotOnMedics, Incura, Evry, ParaNICE), GGZ (HCI CRS), Patient Platforms (Uw Zorg Online, Quli) and E-health (Embloom, Emogy, NICE Connect) - served by a shared Platform and Integration group and a Customer Operations group: six groups and fifteen teams. Each business unit has a small direct staff of business-unit director, label product managers, account managers and marketing who carry the commercial relationship with practices, institutions and GP/pharmacy chains, while its product teams of nine to twelve people (product owner, developers, a designer or tester, and clinically trained specialists such as physiotherapists, psychologists or zorgadministratie experts) own the bricks end to end. Two complicated-subsystem teams encode the Dutch financing rules that change every year - the GDS801 declaration standard and Vecozo flows for paramedics, and the zorgprestatiemodel and Jeugdwet/WMO contracting for GGZ - so that stream-aligned teams do not each re-implement them. Four platform teams provide the care-network connectors (ZorgDomein, ZorgMail, HIS/AIS and hospital systems), the partner API, practice websites and Zorgverlener App, identity and NEN 7510 security, and the multi-tenant cloud runtime with the migration tooling that moves acquired labels into HCI One with no forced deadline. Customer Operations is the largest team by far: implementation consultants, trainers, the support desk and the billing-services desk that handles declaration return messages for practices that outsource their invoicing; because those consultants are themselves users of the platform (impl), every migration defect, ticket pattern or return-message spike reaches the product teams inside the same company. Every team is steward of the data assets its bricks create, so medical files, declarations and consents stay coherent and compliant with AVG, WGBO, NEN 7510, Wegiz and MedMij across every label.

groups.name: Paramedical Business Unit
groups.mission: Own the practice management and EPD proposition for physiotherapy, exercise therapy, speech therapy, occupational therapy, dietetics, foot care and rehabilitation departments across HCI One, FysioRoadmap, SpotOnMedics, Incura, Evry and ParaNICE: the agenda as the central heart of the practice, 24/7 online booking, the web-based dossier with discipline-specific care pathways and KNGF, NVLF and NVD guideline templates, voice-to-text documentation, measurement instruments and PROMs, declarations generated from the agenda and submitted through Vecozo under GDS801, patient invoicing with Mollie, billing services, practice BI and monthly pseudonymised delivery to LDF and Keurmerk. The unit's job is to give the physiotherapist back the working day per week now lost to administration while HCI One absorbs the acquired labels discipline by discipline.

teams.name: Agenda and Booking

The team carries the agenda behaviour of FysioRoadmap, SpotOnMedics, Incura and Evry into one HCI One agenda so that no practice loses a scheduling feature it depends on. Steward of the appointment and group-programme data assets.
teams.mission: Keep every therapist's day fully and correctly booked with as little phone traffic as possible, and make the agenda the single source from which treatments, invoices and declarations flow.

teams.name: Declarations and Payments
teams.description: Own the money flow from registered treatment to money on the account for every paramedical label: the declaration engine that generates GDS801 claims (which replaced PM304 on 1 January 2025) from the agenda and maps them to insurer contracts and the zorgprestatiemodel claim format shared with CRS, the Vecozo gateway with insurance eligibility checks (COV) and return-message processing, patient invoicing with iDEAL and Mollie payment links as SpotOnMedics and Incura offer, accounting export to Twinfield, and the billing-services tooling with which HCI's own desk resubmits rejected claims for practices that outsource invoicing. HCI processed more than EUR 500 million in annual declarations by 2022 and every standard change from PPN, KNGF, ZN, Vektis and Vecozo lands here first. Steward of the declaration-claim, insurance-eligibility-check, return-message, patient-invoice and payment-transaction data assets.
teams.mission: Get every treatment declared and paid first time right, so that a rejection or a return message is the exception a practice never has to touch.

The unit serves a market where waiting times exceed the 14-week Treeknorm in every region and where regulators and financiers demand more data every year, and it is responsible for turning CRS, Embloom and Quli into one integrated GGZ proposition.
